why: A window's chrome panes (Actions, Utilities, Window Options, search) must stay above ANY body content, whatever z-index a canvas host gives its own layers. The window body's PaneHost root is its own stacking context (`isolate`), and every chrome pane is its sibling, never its descendant. Replayed by the Window component suite (structure, jsdom) and by the live `s` matrix probe, whose oracle is Chromium's own hit-testing (`elementFromPoint` over each chip must answer the chip).
liveDefect: Ticket 26/09/23 S15, measured inside `s` on 2026-09-25: raster's `Paint2dHost` paints a transparent full-bleed pointer overlay at `z-30`; the window body was no stacking context, so the overlay out-ranked the chrome panes at `--z-pane: 20` and both raster windows' `Actions` chips were dead to a pointer (`no Actions rail row after unfolding`).
